newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks plummet through support, end sharply off.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks plummet through support, end sharply off.

text.p: A selloff in the property sector sent Hong Kong stocks tumbling through support to end sharply lower on Thursday as investors feared the government may intervene to curb escalating prices in the property market.
The Hang Seng Index slid 202.04 points, or 1.54 percent, to 12,917.09 ending below psychological support at 13,000 points.
Turnover was HK$10.23 billion compared with HK$11.90 billion on Wednesday.
"The two things that are worrying people are affordability (in the property market) and government intervention," said one property analyst at a regional brokerage.
"Investors have seen some dramatic gains in these (property) stocks and they are quite happy with those profits. They want to liquidise them before those profits disappear," he said.
Shares in Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd fell HK$1.25 to HK$70.50, Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd tumbled HK$2.00 to HK$85.00 and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd slid HK$1.75 to HK$64.50.
"It looks like they will remain under pressure but they are very oversold," said Alex Wong, technical analyst at Dharmala Securities. He said a rebound was "very overdue" in the market.
"It is very oversold in the short term. We will probably see some good support around 12,750," Wong said.
The Hang Seng Index has shed 420.26 points, or 3.15 percent, so far this week.
Ricky Tam, research manager at Delta Asia Securities, said interest in second line and red chip stocks had been propping the market up recently.
"But two days ago the second line and red chip stocks peaked and now the whole market is coming down," he said.

Fears of rising interest rates in the United States have also dampened sentiment and brokers said investors were likely to remain cautious until the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting on March 25.
Shenzhen Expressway Co Ltd, which rose 26.14 percent on its market debut on Wednesday, fell HK$0.20 to HK$2.575.
Shares in Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd fell HK$0.05 to HK$11.95 after the Hong Kong flag carrier posted a 27.9 percent surge in 1996 net profit to HK$3.81 billion on Wednesday.
HSBC Holdings Plc dropped HK$3.00 to HK$188.00 and Hang Seng Bank Ltd ended HK$1.00 lower at HK$82.75.
Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd was due to report its 1996 results after the close. The stock rose HK$0.20 to HK$26.90.
